D-13 as amended: a new plan that opens with movement practice (strength class NONE) is identical to the plan without the plane rule; SQ4-C4's 'they do get lat-pulldown or band-pulldown' and SQ4-C9's sweep expectation hold only past movement practice; no copy shown to a class NONE plan suggests plane coverage. A restart from the record keeps class NONE unless the intake facts change (SSCTR-STR-B-03).

D-18, the rule in a plan in force: a slot asks only where the plan was built with it asking; it keeps the configuration it was built with while that fits, prefers nothing while it does not, and returns to it when it fits again; a plan in force never adopts the rule. After a change of strength days that replaces the template of the asking slots (2<->4, 3<->4, 2<->5, 5->2) the plan stops alternating for the rest of its life, also after a return to the original days, and the vertical lifts it was built with can leave it (QRE-STR-C-02: 88 of 308 QRE sequences); the alternation comes back only with a new plan (a plan from the intake or a restart). This is a declared, Founder-accepted cost with no dose, role or stability effect.

No copy for a plan in force claims both planes or alternation unless the current week's rows hold them (SQ4-C7, C8), and none presents the loss after a change of days as a coaching choice. Before any athlete-facing integration, Product/UX decides whether and how the athlete is told that the alternation ended and that a new plan would restore it (QRE-STR-C-02); that is a product and integration matter, not a sporting precondition of synthetic use.

Any later mechanism by which a plan in force adopts the rule is a new SQ-4 c5 question with its own SSCTR review, and must keep R2 criteria 1-3: no slot asks that the plan was not built with, no configuration held only in another role is moved into a MAIN row, and no loaded MAIN row leaves its goal range that stays inside it without the rule.

D-19 (SSCTR-STR-B-02), a known behaviour of plans in force: after a change from two to three or four strength days the vertical configurations a plan was built with can occupy upper accessory slots through the engine's continuity, and at the next block boundary the engine's rotation (B0-C06) can replace them with admissible bodyweight or assisted alternatives of the same plane (STRENGTH 56 of 672 changes, GENERAL 104, RUNNING_SUPPORT 104 with the plane rule alone; all ACCESSORY, week 9, DEVELOPMENT; none on a plane-asking row). This is the frozen rotation, not a plane-rule choice; no copy presents it as a progression or as the plane rule's doing; a change of these counts is a re-review trigger. The missing loading guard in accessory rotation is SSCTR-STR-C-02, routed with A-11 to the Founder; it is not a condition of SQ-4.

QRE-STR-C-01, a restart: restartProgram builds a new plan (the cold start; the record is context only, never a source of doses), so the plane rule asks as in any new plan, and an asking MAIN slot may take a configuration the previous plan used only as an accessory. Accepted as inside SQ-4 for new plans because the new MAIN row is established at the goal's MAIN dose: in 126 such slots over four goals, every first MAIN row is ESTABLISH or BODYWEIGHT, 0 carry a load or dose from the record, 0 differ in sets, repetitions or reserve from the same slot without the plane rule, and 0 externally loaded MAIN rows leave the goal range in nine weeks (QRE: 46 of 780, 0 of 46). Re-review if a restart ever carries prior doses into a new plan, or if the D-14 'earlier sessions of the week' reading or restartIntake changes.

D-3 is the guard's definition (the vertical preference never takes a slot down from the external load it would take without the rule). D-14 holds with the pinned catalog and template order. No claim that vertical work or alternation improves strength, hypertrophy, posture, shoulder health, injury risk or running (SQ4-C8).
